title: MCP Without Polling: Building Reactive Agents with Continuous Queries
abstract: Most MCP servers make agents poll for changes. This talk shows how continuous queries push updates to agents as data changes, cutting latency and wasted tool calls.

title: Your First MCP Server on Kubernetes in 25 Minutes
abstract: A beginner-friendly walkthrough: write a small MCP server, package it as a container, deploy it with a Helm chart and connect an agent to it safely.

title: eBPF para observar agentes sin tocar su código
abstract: Cómo usar eBPF para ver qué hacen los agentes en el kernel: llamadas de red, archivos y procesos, sin instrumentar el código ni reiniciar pods.

title: MCP Is the New Internal API Surface
abstract: Keynote: internal platforms are starting to expose capabilities as MCP tools instead of REST endpoints. What changes for API design, ownership and versioning.

title: GitOps for Prompts and MCP Tools with Argo CD
abstract: Treat prompts, tool definitions and agent configs as declarative resources: review them in pull requests and let Argo CD roll them out and back.

title: Securing the Agentic Tool Layer: A Runtime Defense Framework for MCP Agent Deployments
abstract: A runtime defense framework for MCP deployments: tool allow-lists, argument validation, egress control and audit trails that stop compromised agents from misusing tools.

title: Observabilidad para agentes con OpenTelemetry: del tool call al span
abstract: Cómo trazar cada paso de un agente con OpenTelemetry: prompts, llamadas a herramientas MCP y latencia del modelo, y qué métricas vigilar en producción.

title: Building Governance for Hybrid Architectures for Agentic Systems
abstract: How an enterprise governs agents that span on-prem clusters and SaaS models: policy, identity, approval workflows and the platform team's role.

title: Traffic Handling Patterns in the Agentic Era
abstract: Agents generate bursty, long-lived and fan-out traffic. Case studies of rate limiting, retries and routing patterns for MCP in production.

title: Orchestrating, Discovering, and Autoscaling Distributed Multi-agent AI Systems Natively in K8s
abstract: Run multi-agent systems as Kubernetes-native workloads: service discovery between agents, orchestration with CRDs and autoscaling on queue depth.

title: The Agent Did What? Reconstructing MCP Tool-Call Attacks
abstract: A forensic walkthrough of real MCP tool-call attacks: prompt injection, tool poisoning and data exfiltration, and the logs you need to reconstruct them.

title: Serving LLMs on Kubernetes: GPU Autoscaling with KEDA and vLLM
abstract: Scale vLLM inference servers on GPU nodes with KEDA, warm pools and model caching, and keep cost per token under control.

title: Unlocking Enterprise Knowledge for AI Agents at Scale with MCP
abstract: Connect agents to wikis, tickets and code search through MCP servers, with per-user permissions and caching that holds up at enterprise scale.

title: Architecting the Agentic Data Plane: Scaling MCP
abstract: The architecture behind a data plane for MCP: gateways, session affinity, streaming transports and how to scale tool servers horizontally.

title: Introducing Agent Substrate: Scaling Thousands of Stateful AI Agents on Kubernetes without the Waste
abstract: Agent Substrate runs thousands of stateful agents on Kubernetes by suspending idle ones and restoring them on demand, without a pod per agent.

title: Network Policies with eBPF for Agent Sandboxes
abstract: Use Cilium and eBPF to give every agent sandbox a least-privilege network: DNS-aware egress rules, L7 visibility and fast policy updates.

title: Golden paths para agentes: plataformas internas con Backstage
abstract: Cómo un equipo de plataforma ofrece agentes como producto: plantillas en Backstage, servidores MCP aprobados y despliegue con un clic.

title: What It Took to Write Our Own MCP Gateway
abstract: Why an off-the-shelf proxy was not enough, and what it took to build an MCP gateway: auth, tool routing, quotas and observability.

title: From Alert to Commit: Agentic Incident Resolution
abstract: An agent that takes an alert, gathers metrics, logs and traces through MCP tools, finds the cause and opens a pull request with the fix.

title: Building and Maintaining Production-Ready SDKs with LLMs
abstract: Lessons from generating and maintaining SDKs with LLMs: test harnesses, review loops and where agents still need a human.

title: Stop Wasting GPUs: Building a Workload-Aware Caching Proxy for Agentic AI Workflows
abstract: Agentic workflows resend the same context again and again. A workload-aware caching proxy that reuses KV cache and cuts GPU time.

title: Toward AI-Native Platform Operations: Releasing 100+ Microservices with Agentic AI
abstract: How a platform team uses agents to release more than 100 microservices: change risk scoring, automated rollbacks and human approval gates.

title: I Rebuilt Agent Memory Three Times. The Third Time I Treated It Like Data.
abstract: Three designs for agent memory, from prompt stuffing to a proper data layer with schemas, retention and retrieval exposed over MCP.

title: Protocol Solved, Design Still Open: Domain-Driven Design for MCP Servers
abstract: MCP fixed the wire protocol, not tool design. Apply domain-driven design to decide what an MCP server exposes and how tools are named and scoped.

title: Detonation and Isolation: Hardening Kubernetes Runtimes for Agents
abstract: Run untrusted agent code safely: gVisor and Kata sandboxes, seccomp profiles and what to do when an agent tries to break out.

title: GitOps a escala con agentes que abren pull requests
abstract: Agentes que proponen cambios a los manifiestos y Argo CD que los aplica: cómo revisar, limitar y auditar los PR que escribe una máquina.
